examples.japanese: {手榴弾|しゅりゅうだん}を{投|な}げる。
{不発|ふはつ}の{手榴弾|しゅりゅうだん}が{工事現場|こうじげんば}で{見|み}つかった。
examples.english: An unexploded hand grenade was found at a construction site.

examples.japanese: {戦争|せんそう}{映画|えいが}では{手榴弾|しゅりゅうだん}のピンを{抜|ぬ}くシーンがよく{描|えが}かれるが、{実際|じっさい}にはもっと{複雑|ふくざつ}な{手順|てじゅん}がある。
examples.english: War movies often depict scenes of pulling the pin on a grenade, but in reality the procedure is more complex.

notes:
Composed of {手|しゅ} (hand) + {榴弾|りゅうだん} (shrapnel shell). A small explosive weapon designed to be thrown by hand. The word appears frequently in military history, news about unexploded ordnance, and war-themed media.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {手榴弾|しゅりゅうだん}を{投|な}げる: to throw a grenade
- {手榴弾|しゅりゅうだん}のピンを{抜|ぬ}く: to pull the pin on a grenade
- {不発|ふはつ}{手榴弾|しゅりゅうだん}: unexploded grenade
- {手榴弾|しゅりゅうだん}が{爆発|ばくはつ}する: a grenade explodes

PRONUNCIATION:
Sometimes also read as てりゅうだん, though しゅりゅうだん is the standard reading.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {榴弾|りゅうだん}: shrapnel shell, fragmentation round — the larger artillery projectile
- {爆弾|ばくだん}: bomb — a general term for explosive devices
- {地雷|じらい}: landmine — an explosive buried in the ground
